subject.title: RFC: Readiness Conditions and Standard Hosting Profiles

question: Which subset of canonical conditions, compatibility projections, plugin providers, hosting profiles, activation identity, and release-conformance obligations should OpenClaw accept in the initial RFC?
rationale: The document and linked implementation establish technical feasibility, but automated review cannot commit the project to a permanent public API, fail-closed policy, upgrade boundary, and release-support promise.

options.title: Accept Proven Foundation
options.body: Approve canonical core conditions and compatibility projections first, while deferring broader activation and release-conformance obligations to follow-up RFC decisions.

options.title: Accept Complete Roadmap
options.body: Approve the full response, plugin, configuration, identity, profile, and release-support contract as one long-term commitment.

options.title: Decline Core Ownership
options.body: Keep hosting-readiness composition downstream or plugin-owned rather than establishing this core support contract.

recommendation.title: Accept Proven Foundation
recommendation.body: Approve canonical core conditions and compatibility projections first, while deferring broader activation and release-conformance obligations to follow-up RFC decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: Git blame and merged history show the strongest available ownership of this repository's RFC acceptance process and cross-cutting policy review.
